setup: No. 5 Texas (9–2) enters the Lone Star Showdown after five straight victories, most recently a 45–3 win over Arkansas. Texas A&M (4–7) has dropped four straight, but a rivalry game at Kyle Field offers a chance to disrupt the Longhorns' playoff ambitions.

things.title: Manning's efficiency
things.body: Arch Manning completed 21 of 25 passes for 287 yards and accounted for three touchdowns against Arkansas. A&M needs to force longer drives and disrupt his rhythm without giving up easy throws.

things.title: The Aggies' quarterback decision
things.body: Brady Hart made his first start against Oklahoma and completed eight of 20 attempts for 131 yards. Mike Elko has not committed to a starter for the rivalry; whichever quarterback plays needs manageable third downs against Colin Simmons and the Texas pass rush.

things.title: Turnovers and field position
things.body: Texas defensive back Jelani McDonald recorded four interceptions and a pick-six across two games. The Aggies need clean possessions and a physical run game to limit the short fields that could let Texas take control.

breakdown.bottom_line: Texas has the momentum and postseason stakes, while A&M has home-field energy and a chance to salvage its season. Protection, early-down execution and avoiding turnovers will determine whether the Aggies can keep the rivalry competitive.
